society.title: Mini-Ani as a society of mind
society.question: Who decides how fast Cinderella is?
society.intro: The Mini-Ani as Minsky's Society of Mind: its Choice Points are split into thirteen small choosers, each choosing one thing about everyone, like their speed. Nobody chooses everything. The choosers work in agencies, and a Gatherer puts their answers together. Same rules, same story: is it the same film?
questions: Who decides how fast Cinderella is? Open the Choosers agency, then Speed (Look inside).
Play the same story in the Mini-Ani. Is the film the same? Why might it be?
Find Ani's “deadly embrace” in a chooser's answer: which two choices waited for each other?
The Gatherer says a subtle film needs someone who sees all of a character at once. Which agent in the Mini-Ani does? Does it matter that nobody here does?
Some rules speak to a whole agency. Which ones? How many messages does one of them send?
openers: What does the Speed chooser know about Cinderella?
Why might a society have no boss?

starts.label: Cinderella, as Ani told it
starts.value:
Cinderella is shy, good, friendly, hardworking, beautiful and shabby.
The Stepmother is mean, selfish, strong and evil.
The Godmother is good, kind, strong, pretty and magical.
The Prince is good, stubborn, determined, beautiful and strong.
The Stepmother dominates Cinderella. Cinderella obeys the Stepmother. The Godmother helps Cinderella.
Scene 1: Cinderella is shy. The Stepmother dominates Cinderella.
Scene 2: The Stepmother keeps Cinderella from the Prince. Cinderella becomes sad.
Scene 3: The Godmother changes Cinderella from shabby to elegant. Cinderella becomes happy.
Scene 4: Cinderella changes from shy to bold. Cinderella meets the Prince.

starts.label: The shy one joins in
starts.value:
Tom is shy, kind and graceful.
Sam is friendly, strong and determined.
Ivy is friendly, kind and beautiful.
Sam helps Ivy.
Scene 1: Tom is shy. Sam meets Ivy.
Scene 2: Ivy helps Tom. Tom becomes happy.
Scene 3: Tom changes from shy to friendly. Tom meets Sam.

starts.label: The grumpy one becomes kind
starts.value:
The Wolf is mean, strong and grumpy.
The Lamb is shy, good and graceful.
The Owl is good, kind and magical.
The Wolf dominates the Lamb. The Owl helps the Lamb.
Scene 1: The Lamb is shy. The Wolf dominates the Lamb.
Scene 2: The Owl changes the Wolf from grumpy to good. The Wolf becomes sad.
Scene 3: The Wolf changes from mean to kind. The Wolf meets the Lamb. The Lamb becomes happy.

agents.name: Cast
agents.role: reads a story and sends it one scene at a time
agents.note: reads a story and sends it one scene at a time
agents.pseudocode:
the story's own words: "{is}", "{and}", "{the}", "{Scene}", "{changes}", "{from}", "{to}", "{becomes}"
"X is a, b and c" before the scenes says what X is like; in a scene it shows that X is a
"A does something to B" before the scenes is how they get on; in a scene it is something that happens
{helps, likes, loves} make two characters friends
"A changes B from X to Y", "A changes from X to Y" and "A becomes Y" change someone, but {happy, sad} are feelings
at the start, read the story, and send scene 1 with everyone, so the experts suggest values for the whole cast
after each film, send the next scene: who is on stage, what happens, and how they get on
for someone who changes in a scene, also send a stand-in, "X {after}", with the new words; from then on X has them
when the Renderer says a film didn't run, say so, and go on to the next scene
after the last scene, end the story, and say "The end."
name any sentence I can't read; with nobody or no scenes, say how to write a story, send the story back (for a Reader), and wait for another

agents.name: Speed
agents.note: chooses everyone's speed, from the suggestions about it
agents.pseudocode:
wait for the scene and the experts' suggestions: {5} messages, or until nobody else has anything to say
I choose one thing about everyone the Cast says is being chosen: {speed}, which is {slow/fast}, compared as {slower/faster}
the levels are {low, medium, high}; “{same} …” means the same as someone else's
a suggestion is a word with {a bit} (weaker), {very} (stronger) or {not} (rules it out) before it
a suggestion counts its strength (a bit 1, plain 2, very 3) times where it came from:
  the character's own word {3}, a word meaning the same {2}, the opposite of a word {1}, a comparison {4}, the film's taste {1}
I listen only to suggestions about my thing: the rest are for the other choosers
choose for the film's focus first, then in the Cast's order:
  a comparison like “faster than X” waits for X's value, then rules out X's value and below
  if two choices wait for each other, the first goes without its comparison (Ani's “deadly embrace”)
  the film's variety adds a weak suggestion: low variety my value used most so far, high the least, medium the middle one
  a value is ruled out if what is against it is at least as strong as what is for it
  if one value is more than {2} times as strong as the next, it wins
  if not, low and high meet in the middle, unless the middle is ruled out; then the stronger wins, or the one said first
  if nobody suggested anything, it is medium; if everything is ruled out, a comparison keeps its own direction
remember the values; a stand-in gets the variety and comparisons its character had, and then its value becomes the character's
send everyone's value and why, and the suggestions I understood, for the Gatherer

scenarios.name: it chooses its thing for everyone being chosen, and leaves the rest to the other choosers
a comparison waits for the other's value: faster than Bob, who is slow
two choices that wait for each other: the first goes without its comparison (Ani's “deadly embrace”)
when nobody is being chosen, everyone keeps what was chosen before
